New York has always been a leader in protecting reproductive, health, and rights and I want to thank Speaker Adams and my colleagues in the Women’s Caucus for putting forward such a comprehensive and important package of bills that will both protect our existing rights and improve access to abortion care in this post-Roe era. The bills that we’re passing today should act as a model for cities throughout the rest of the country for what we can and must do to protect our basic right to bodily autonomy and increased access to important healthcare. I am particularly proud of my bills, Intro 506, that I introduced with the Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson to implement an outreach and education program to inform New Yorkers about the deceptive

New York City’s abortions protections are underutilized, with many New Yorkers simply not aware they exist, and 474-A addresses this information gap by requiring the City to conduct language-accessible public education and media campaigns about existing protections. These include the right to access the health facilities without harassment and prohibitions against employment or housing discrimination on the basis of reproductive health decision. Additionally, following the Dobbs decision, there will be an influx of people travelling to New York City for reproductive care. People seeking transaffirming hormone treatment will also travel here for care as well. These folks are vulnerable to civil suits for receiving medical procedures that are legal in our city, but illegal in their home state or municipality. And so, 475-A addresses this issue by establishing these suits as interference with medical care and allowing people to countersue under New York City law. If the countersuit prevails, the plaintiff will be awarded $10,000 in damages and also awarded
